rationale: Lyc. noun introducing the topic-clause 'that you may see no sins among them.' Likely a variant on the ⲱⲡ/ⲍⲉⲡ family ('reckon, judge, matter'). Functions discourse-syntactically as a topic-noun rather than a content-rich term. Confidence moderate; flag for parallel attestations.

Lyc. qualitative or stative form predicated of ⲍⲏⲧ 'heart.' Context (contrast with ⲙⲛⲧⲧⲱⲛ 'contention') supports a sense of inward equanimity or firmness. Lexeme not securely attested elsewhere in this corpus; possible relations: ⲛⲁϣⲧ 'be hard/firm,' ⲛⲟⲩⲃⲥ̄ 'shake/agitate' (would require negation). Confidence low.

rationale: Lyc. reduplicated verb describing the holy ones' mutual disturbance under the influence of the indwelling Old Man. Reduplication suggests iterative/intensive aspect. Possibly cognate with ϭⲗⲟⲡ 'complain' or ϭⲗⲟⲙⲗⲙ̄ 'rage.' Confidence low.
ⲛⲧⲁϩ functioning as emphatic intensifier within a prohibition (ⲙ̄ⲡⲱⲣ). Possibly a Lyc. reflex of ⲛ̄ⲧⲟϥ 'indeed' or a reduced causative-conjunctive ⲛⲧⲁⲣⲉ-. Confidence low.

Attention-getting interjection introducing the imperative ϯ-ⲍⲧⲏⲕ 'set your heart.' Etymology unclear — possibly Coptic interjection or Greek loanword (τοίνυν 'therefore'?) garbled. Function-translated. Confidence low.
Adverbial qualifier in the Nazoraean's challenge: 'do you trust in him X or not?' Likely an adverb of veracity/sincerity. Possibly Lyc. for ⲟⲛⲧⲱⲥ or ϩⲁⲡⲗⲱⲥ. Confidence moderate.
Closes the binary question 'truly or not ϩⲍⲁⲩ.' Functions as an enclitic emphasizer ('in any wise' / 'at all'). Etymology uncertain. Confidence low.
